purpose: A machine-readable map of what has been ruled out and how tightly, so a session can ask what is already closed before spending effort reopening it.

verdicts.no_evidence: tested and bounded: the effect is inside what the sample can resolve
verdicts.resolvable: the effect exceeds what the sample can resolve and clears its bootstrap
verdicts.below_cost: real and untradeable: the effect nets out below the round-trip cost
verdicts.underpowered: not testable on this data; the entry names what it would take
verdicts.survives_screens: cleared every screen applied — treat as a candidate, not a rule
verdicts.skipped: could not be computed; the reason is recorded

how_to_read.smallest_resolvable_effect: The smallest effect the sample could have separated. A null is only as strong as this number: 'no evidence' with a wide bound rules out very little, and saying so is the point.
how_to_read.extending: Add a hypothesis to a sweep runner, or add a study. This file is derived and regenerated; editing it by hand would make it drift from the evidence.

data_gaps.gap: The repository holds 12 weekly CFTC rows (2026-06-02 onward) because the weekly fetcher keeps a rolling window, not a history. This hypothesis needs years. CFTC publishes the full Commitments of Traders history free; archiving it is a prerequisite for any positioning hypothesis, and it is the single cheapest way to open a family this dataset currently cannot test.

entries.family: none — bar-level pattern mining, independent of S1 and S2
entries.claim: XAUUSD 30-minute pattern mining — three artefacts and one regularity
entries.reason: None. Candlestick patterns, weekly slot selection, round numbers and multi-bar discretised sequences are all artefacts — of drift, selection, coincidence and enumeration respectively. Daily extreme timing survives a shuffled-returns null with stable magnitudes across all three periods, and is a non-directional timing observation rather than a rule. Revision 2 also records two non-statistical screens, ablation and mirror, that caught candidates which sign-consistency let through. Revision 3 (2026-08-23) removes a directional sentence from impact.md: the surviving result is that extremes cluster at the same hours, not that lows form in the Asian morning and highs at the New York session.

entries.family: none — price-series structure, independent of S1 and S2
entries.claim: XAUUSD intraday range accumulation — the shape holds, the clock moves, and the level does not
entries.reason: None. The 30-minute range profile is real against a shuffled-returns null (family permutation p 0.005 in all three periods) and its shape is stable, but three caveats bound its use: the busiest US half hour is 08:30 ET and moves an hour on the Taipei clock twice a year (4.51% vs 0.88% at Taipei 20:30), the level is non-stationary with the Asian share up 12 points since 2024, and a busy Asian morning carries no information about the range still to come (Spearman -0.074). After 23:30 Taipei the median session is finished. Descriptive and non-directional; no live effect granted.

entries.claim: S1 V3.9 Bollinger %B at entry — the strongest effect in the programme, and why it is not a filter
entries.reason: None. Entries above the upper band win 73.17% on n=82 against a 55.93% baseline, clearing family permutation (p=0.003), a moving-block bootstrap (90% CI 10.96-29.64, above zero in every resample), out-of-sample (65.12/81.25/82.61 while the baseline decayed 56.76/57.63/51.58), a continuous dose-response (Spearman 0.839, still rising inside the bucket) and a momentum ablation (positive in all three terciles). It is the only claim in the programme to clear all of them. Filtering on it nevertheless loses money: %B>1.0 keeps 17.4% of entries and 44% of total return, and best win rate never coincides with best return. Its place is as decision-time information, not a gate. CORRECTED 2026-09-01 by RS-XAUUSD-20260901-001: the %B label was read from the entry bar, which closes thirty minutes after the intrabar fill. Re-run on the last completed bar the gap falls from 20.86 to 9.26 points against a bound rising from 16.9 to 20.28, permutation p from 0.0003 to 0.0748, and the dose response is no longer monotone. This search space no longer has a survivor — it is open with a wide bound, not refuted, and the programme now has no surviving positive finding.

entries.family: none — hypothesis sweep on the price series
entries.claim: Twenty hypotheses, zero survivors — and a registry so the next twenty do not repeat them
entries.reason: None. Twenty hypotheses — six of them published claims about gold specified by others — through one harness: 18 no evidence, 1 untestable, 1 real but below cost, 0 survivors, family permutation p=0.928. Two method results carry further than the twenty answers. A lookahead bug produced the study's strongest number (+1.5704% at p=0.000) by comparing a session's high to its own opening range and predicting that same session; corrected, the effect is -0.0132% and the family p moves from 0.0675 to 0.928. And a cost screen must compare the NET effect to the resolution bound, not the gross effect to cost: the dead-zone drift passes the soft test and nets +0.0022% against a 0.0147% bound. Primary output is research/null_results.json, which puts every closed search space in one queryable shape with its resolution bound attached.

entries.claim: CFTC positioning — 31 weeks cannot answer it, and the publication lag says why that matters less than it looks
entries.reason: None. 31 weekly COT reports transcribed from source screenshots and verified against the official CSV (132 of 132 field-values matched). The report settles Tuesday and publishes Friday, so Wed-Fri is already history when it lands — a built-in placebo window almost no COT research has. Across 14 hypotheses the two windows correlate at 0.091 and agree in sign 7 of 14; of the five largest historical effects, two flip after publication and three shrink to zero. Nothing is resolvable: weekly return SD is 3.99% and 31 weeks resolve about 4 points, while every effect is under 2.2. The stated producer/merchant hypothesis points the other way (-0.94% vs +1.23%), far inside the noise. A hedging mechanism was asserted for the decomposition and withdrawn the same day: the correlation with the concurrent week is 0.062, and both window differences (-1.672 +/- 0.980 and -0.514 +/- 0.735) have intervals containing zero, so which window the effect lives in is itself unresolvable. CFTC publishes ~880 weeks of history free; archiving it is the unlock.

entries.family: none — selection methodology tested on CFTC positioning
entries.claim: Three stated claims tested on 274 weeks — one is circular, one measures the period, one buys win rate with return
entries.reason: None. CFTC disaggregated history downloaded with permission (503 gold weeks from 2017, verified 279/279 against the source screenshots), giving 274 usable weeks against 31. Claim 1, Monday sweeps the low then rises: a 30.1-point gap that falls to 1.35 once the condition is read at Monday's close instead of inside the window it predicts — the second lookahead of this kind in two days. Claim 2, >50% win rate is alpha: the Mon+Tue baseline is 45.6% in the sample's first half and 54.3% in the second, so the same threshold beats the market in one period and loses in the other; 1 of 182 conditions cleared 50% in the first half against 80% of all of them in the second, and win rate correlates -0.077 across halves. Claim 3, consensus: correct about the effect. Five of six positioning votes gives 62.5% against 48.8%, survives walk-forward, and loses money — payoff ratio 0.55 against 1.22, taking 11.7% of opportunities for -7.8% of return. Third independent demonstration that win rate is purchasable and the currency is expectancy.

entries.family: none — 1OZ futures accumulation and position sizing
entries.claim: Four monthly buys of 1OZ gold futures held to March — what history allows and what the arithmetic allows are different numbers
S2 V3.2 — the Asia session is a third of the trades and a tenth of the return, and removing it costs money
entries.reason: None. Removing the Asia session raises every per-trade measure and lowers total return by 10.43 points; corrected for having searched four sessions the gain is p=0.0549, inside what dropping the worst of four arbitrary groups produces. Recorded as a candidate for prospective testing because the gap is stable across both chronological periods.

entries.claim: S2 V3.2 — the decline is in every session, not in Asia, and S1 did not share it
entries.reason: None. The S2 decline is entirely within-session (101.6% of the change) and Asia's fall is the third largest of four, so there is no Asia phenomenon. S1 over the identical window did not decline, so it is not market-wide either. Attribution to the regime change is the best available reading, not established: p=0.0619 on the decline itself.

entries.family: S1 AweWithBB V3.9 / S2 Hammer V3.2
entries.claim: Pullback versus chase — tested directly, it fails, and it was never a shared pattern
entries.reason: None. Family p=0.3588 against a frozen 0.05. The effect is S2-only — S1's largest correlation across five horizons is 0.0403 with two positive — so the shared-direction reading that made it the top candidate does not survive direct measurement. S2's consistency (5/5 negative, 5/5 holding out of sample) is noted for a prospective registration.

entries.claim: S1 V3.9 — the first bar predicts the outcome, and acting on it destroys value
entries.reason: None. The first bar's mark clears its own resolution bound (22.47 points against 13.13) and strengthens out of sample, and all eight cut-or-halve rules built on it lose return, the best by 12.70 points. The flagged group is weaker but still profitable, so acting on the flag discards about 94 eventual winners.

entries.claim: S1 V3.9 — sizing up on %B does not help, and the signal may be measured on a bar that has not closed
entries.reason: None yet, and one open verification. Sizing up on %B does not help: best gain 0.78 points at equal volatility, family p=0.2823, and every raw gain reverses under risk adjustment. Separately, the published %B win-rate gap appears to be labelled on the entry bar, which closes after the intrabar fill; measured on the last completed bar it is 6.01 points rather than 17.79. RS-XAUUSD-20260823-002 and -20260824-006 need re-running with entry_index - 1.

entries.claim: Buy the month open, sell the month close — one month clears its bound, and only on the short sample
entries.reason: None. Across 48 month-by-series cells exactly one clears its own resolution bound — XAUUSD January on daily 2008+, by 0.033 percentage points — and it does not clear on the 1980+ sample. Separately: weekly-derived month boundaries disagree with daily by a mean 4.48 win-rate points for XAUUSD and 4.76 for TX, which is a caution about every seasonality result computed on weekly bars, RS-TX-20260728-001 included.

entries.claim: The surviving %B finding was measured on a bar that had not closed — re-run, it fails every screen
entries.reason: None of its own. Consequential for RS-XAUUSD-20260823-002 and -20260824-006: with the %B label on the last completed bar rather than the bar the fill happened inside, the gap falls from 20.86 to 9.26 points against a bound rising from 16.9 to 20.28, permutation p from 0.0003 to 0.0748, and the dose response is no longer monotone. The unmodified path reproduces the published numbers exactly. Amending those two records changes a conclusion and awaits a decision.

entries.claim: Scoring the weekly report — the rubric, and why two editions cannot produce a hit rate
entries.reason: None. A frozen scoring rubric for the weekly report plus the two editions whose weeks have finished. Two editions cannot separate any hit rate from a coin flip (bound 99.07 points against a maximum possible 50), and the single direction hit depends on how a 38/38 tie is broken. Mean Brier 0.7157 beats every constant baseline (best 1.0) and is the measure worth accumulating.

entries.claim: Hurst is the estimator, the range boundary is arithmetic, and the range timing was already known
entries.reason: None. Hurst is 0.5502 against a shuffled control of 0.5491, so the apparent persistence is estimator bias and long memory does not explain the direction/volatility asymmetry. The intraday range extension is arithmetic (1 minus realised in every decile). The range timing is real — back-loaded against a within-day shuffle, turning at 23:00 Taipei — and confirms RS-XAUUSD-20260819-001's independently found 21:00-23:00 cluster.

entries.family: S1 AweWithBB V3.9 / S2 Hammer V3.2
entries.claim: After an S1 stop-loss — the S2 that follows is better than average, and skipping it costs 35% of the book
entries.reason: None yet. Skipping the S2 that follows an S1 stop-loss, and the S1 after it, costs total return at every window tested — 59.85 points of a 173.02 baseline at 48 hours. The S2 after a stop wins 60.56% against 42.57% and returns 1.008% against 0.3818%, holding and strengthening out of sample, but the 17.99-point gap does not clear its 21.66-point bound. The cost of skipping is established; the reason to take is not. CORRECTED 2026-09-01 by RS-XAUUSD-20260901-005: the stated mechanism does not survive a take-profit placebo; the cost of skipping is unaffected.

entries.family: S1 AweWithBB V3.9 / S2 Hammer V3.2
entries.claim: The stop-loss was standing in for the exit — a placebo test that overturns its own study's reading
entries.reason: None of its own; corrects RS-XAUUSD-20260901-004's reading. S2 after an S1 stop wins 55.36% against 47.76% after an S1 take-profit — 7.60 points against a 25.32-point bound, p=0.1571 — while S2 with no S1 exit nearby wins 36.00%. Proximity to an S1 exit, not the exit type, is doing the work. The earlier study's decision conclusion is unaffected.

entries.claim: Volatility does not explain the exit-proximity effect, and neither does anything else — it is one cell
entries.reason: None. Volatility does not explain the exit-proximity effect — 79.4% of the gap survives stratification — but the effect is not established either: the tercile gaps are +6.20, -20.51 and +52.50, the middle reverses, and the high tercile rests on twenty trades winning 10.0%. The confound runs opposite to the assumption: co-activity falls as volatility rises, 82.69% to 61.54%.

entries.claim: Fibonacci staged entry for the September-to-January window buys everything at once, or nothing at all
entries.reason: None. The return comparison does not resolve: the paired difference is -2.227 percentage points against a resolution bound of 4.59 on 18 cycles. What is established is that the rule does not stage the entry — fills are decided by where the August close sits inside the year's range, so it commits everything at once when gold is weak into September and holds back when gold is strong. Three of eighteen cycles never invested at all.
